title: fix(sse): streaming chunking/framing fixes for partial JSON + token/event ordering
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming chunking/framing that could emit partial JSON tokens out of order; improves OpenAI compatibility for function/tool call streamed events; no behavioral API changes expected.
description:
Motivation: Several downstream clients (including the OpenAI-compat SDK and the TS SDK streaming helpers) observed malformed partial-JSON payloads when the SSE encoder split on byte/line boundaries. Root causes: (1) the streaming encoder sometimes emitted token event chunks where JSON structural delimiters ("}" and "]") were split across frames, and (2) we relied on newline-delimiting heuristics that reordered token events under high concurrency. This surfaced as partial JSON objects or arrays arriving in incorrect order, which broke structured-output consumers and function-calling logic.

What this change does: consolidates chunking logic in the SSE encoder to preserve JSON token/event boundaries, normalizes delimiter handling so that partial bytes that form JSON punctuation are always emitted together, and adds an explicit token ordering guarantee (per-request sequence numbers) on the event stream. Also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to ensure function_call events are emitted atomically and with the same framing semantics as normal messages.

Scope: runtime/sse encoder, openai-compat streaming adapter, typescript sdk streaming helper tests, unit + e2e tests. Small follow-ups: a comment in the streaming RFC, and a runtime metrics counter for malformed-frame drops (should be zero after this).

Implementation notes (high level): - Introduced a small state machine in sse/encoder that buffers up to the last UTF-8 codepoint boundary and JSON punctuation characters before flushing. This avoids producing frames that split "}," or "]}" sequences. - Added per-event monotonic sequence numbers attached to SSE comments (e.g. ":seq=42") to make consumer-side reordering detectable and to ease debugging. - Modified openai_compat/streaming_adapter to aggregate function_call tokens until the call object is complete before emitting a final "event:function_call" SSE message, preserving the prior behavior expected by SDKs. - Added targeted unit tests for edge cases (multi-byte UTF-8 punctuation, long-running KV cache streaming, and high-concurrency interleaving). - Fixed a race in runtime/stream_router where a canceled request could still publish a pending prefix chunk.

Testing and CI: unit tests initially failed on a new edge case (multi-byte punctuation at 4k boundaries) — addressed by improving the buffer boundary logic. End-to-end tests include a simulated TS SDK streaming consumer that reconstructs partial JSON objects; all e2e scenarios pass in CI. Performance impact: microbenchmarks show ~0.2% added CPU in worst-case streaming paths due to the small state machine; overall latency unchanged for normal requests.

Backwards compatibility: consumers relying on a non-zero chance of split punctuation frames will see no change except improved correctness. No API shape changes.

Related: Linear ENG-1923 (streaming stability), ENG-2011 (openai-compat streaming correctness).

review_comments: Alex Rivera: Can you add a short comment explaining why sequence numbers are added as SSE comments rather than custom fields? We should avoid breaking clients that parse event data directly.
Priya Nair: The openai compat change looks correct but please add an integration test that verifies function_call is emitted as a single event under the TS SDK consumer (we rely on that in prod).
Sam Patel: Are there any increased memory allocations for large streaming sessions? We should document worst-case buffer size and add a safeguard cap.
author_responses: Maya Chen: Added comment in encoder.rs explaining the choice; sequence numbers are emitted as SSE comments to avoid coupling the data payload format with transport metadata.
Maya Chen: Added the TS SDK integration test (sdk-typescript/src/streaming/reconstructor.test.ts) per Priya's request.
Maya Chen: Added a 64KB soft cap to the per-request buffer with metrics and a fallback that emits an error event; documented in the RFC and added a unit test.
